articleTitle: Applications and onward development of ANSI/IEEE Std 1149.1
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Application and Development of the Boundary-Scan Standard
abstract: Many companies, encouraged by the recent introduction of ANSI/IEEE Standard 1149.1 are starting to use boundary-scan techniques for testing loaded PWBs. Applications and future developments of this standard are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Application and Development of the Boundary-Scan Standard
abstract: In December 1989, a proposal was put forward jointly by Plessey Roke Manor Research, British Aerospace, and Southampton University under the Advanced Technology Programme of the IED. This proposal was approved, and was intended to start in July 1990; unforeseen circumstances intervened, however, so that essentially the same project will now be run with Plessey, ICL, and Southampton, and is expected to start in January 1991. The overall objectives of this programme of work are: (a) to study the opportunities offered by using the principles of boundary scan to test PCBs; (b) to establish the limitations imposed by practical circuit designs in which not all circuit elements have boundary scan facilities; and (c) to develop CAD software tools that will automatically overlay the necessary test structures onto an integrated circuit design, and to compile test programs conforming to the 1149.1 protocol.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An initial design study of the use of boundary scan to simplify system test (guided weapons)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Application and Development of the Boundary-Scan Standard
abstract: The Defence Division (DD) of Thorn EMI is currently developing a servo-system for a gimballed transceiver as part of a seeker system to be installed in a missile. In order to enhance the test access at the component, board and assembly levels, the use of boundary scan circuits in an ASIC implementation has been addressed. The purpose of this paper is not to review the detailed benefits which have accrued for the particular application, but to illustrate and expand on the system level test strategies which can be adopted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bridging fault algorithms for a boundary scan board
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Application and Development of the Boundary-Scan Standard
abstract: Although the introduction of boundary scan reduces the need for in-circuit testing via a bed-of-nails fixture, the time taken to load a test vector serially places a new premium on minimising the number of test vectors. In addition, net testing via a boundary scan has to rely on detecting standard voltage level changes rather than the resistance-related tests possible with in-circuit testing. This paper examines these problems in the context of net bridging faults and describes efficient detection and diagnosis algorithms based on a Pin-Adjacency fault model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Boundary scan design for a memory controller
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Application and Development of the Boundary-Scan Standard
abstract: A boundary-scan design that fully conforms to the IEEE 1149.1 standard has been incorporated in MEMC2, a complete memory and system controller for ARM-based systems. MEMC2 provides a two level memory management system: Level 1 Page Tables are stored on-chip for improved access speed while the larger Level 2 Tables are stored in main memory. An on-chip 64-entry Translation Lookaside Buffer of Level 2 Page Tables further improves performance by caching most recently used translations. The chip can control a large DRAM memory system; it also provides support for static RAM and ROM and provides a video interface and seven on-chip DMA channels. This device has recently been fabricated by VLSI Technology in their 1.0 mu m double-level metal CMOS process and it is fully functional.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experience of designing JTAG ASICS within System X
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Application and Development of the Boundary-Scan Standard
abstract: Describes some of the experience gained when using the Boundary Scan technique, as proposed by the Joint Test Action Group (JTAG), for Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) design at GEC Plessey Telecommunication (GPT) in Poole; and offers some thoughts on the advantages and disadvantages of the JTAG method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
